findings.description: The original code only fell back to field_name when data_key was None. Using `or` also treats an empty string as missing. A field declared with data_key="" is a valid explicit key, since the Field code only checks `is not None`. With this change, Pluck would serialize and deserialize under field_name instead of "", while the inner schema uses "". The two sides then disagree, which breaks the round trip and the error keys.
findings.suggestion: Restore the explicit None check: `return only_field.data_key if only_field.data_key is not None else self.field_name`.
findings.title: Falsy data_key (empty string) now falls back to field_name
